cases.name: asymmetric_m_gt_n
cases.why: M != N, so an operand swap in the accumulate is NOT shape-safe: this is the case that would have caught the reversed operand order

cases.name: asymmetric_n_gt_m
cases.why: the other asymmetry, so a swap fails in both directions

cases.name: bias
cases.why: bias initialised into the accumulator by broadcast rather than added afterwards, which is the hardware's own init path

cases.name: bias_narrow_m
cases.why: bias broadcast with a single output row: the init writes all rows whether or not they are read

cases.name: full_range_int8
cases.why: full-range int8 operands over a long reduction: the largest magnitudes the datapath can be handed. It does NOT overflow, and cannot -- see ACC_OVERFLOW_UNREACHABLE_ABOVE_K, which is why no corpus case tests the missing saturation

cases.name: requant_square
cases.why: the epilogue on a square tile: the base case for scale/round/clamp/narrow being bit-exact against numpy

cases.name: requant_narrow_m
cases.why: epilogue with a single output row -- the readout writes one row and the narrowing must follow it, not the whole tile

cases.name: requant_narrow_n
cases.why: epilogue on a single output column: a per-column multiplier indexed wrongly is invisible when there is more than one column to average over

cases.name: requant_tail
cases.why: epilogue across a short row tile AND a short column tile, so the narrowing is exercised where the tiling loop's bounds are ragged

cases.name: requant_saturating
cases.why: full-range operands over a long reduction, so the accumulator is large and the clamp actually fires -- the cases above mostly do not reach it, and a clamp that never runs is a clamp that is not tested

cases.name: requant_with_bias
cases.why: bias broadcast into the accumulator AND the epilogue applied after it: the two halves of the dispatch composed, which is the L4 rung

cases.name: workload_ffn_up
cases.why: spectformer's FFN up-projection shape (12 of them in the model, the joint largest contributor): M=196 is not a multiple of any tile edge, so every tile column ends in a short row tile

cases.name: workload_ffn_down
cases.why: the FFN down-projection (12 of them): the same short M with a narrower N, so the tail lands at a different place in the tiling loop

cases.name: workload_attn_proj
cases.why: the fused QKV projection (8 of them): N=768 is a whole number of tiles at every edge, isolating the M tail from the N tail

cases.name: workload_im2col
cases.why: the patch-embedding contraction: the ONLY routed shape whose N is not a multiple of the operand alignment, so it is the case that would catch a right-operand row stride the datapath cannot fetch

cases.name: workload_classifier
cases.why: the classifier head: M=1 at a large N, i.e. a vecmat over many tile columns. The M=1 probes above use a single tile; this one runs the tiling loop with one live row throughout, which is where a row-index bug in the readout would show
